svg.text: Ch'alish P'ilam, the ceremonial hand — the canon and a pilot
Every glyph is its own picture, drawn whole inside a cushion that always stands round it. Two brushes: the contour brush, 32 units, and the detail brush, 20.
Heads face the line's start. The kit of recurring parts gives the hand its look; no glyph is built from a skeleton. Drawn from tools/chalish-pilam/ceremonial.py.
a narrow affix before a sign
a flattened affix over a sign
An inscription in paired columns: read A1, B1, A2, B2, down the pair
a lord, the jaguar, on the thirteenth;
the sun over the sacred peak; the moon on the water; the sun
Blocks beside Monaspace Neon at 48 and 24 px
